## Où j'en suis

The SRE take-home now lives in its own private repo, `kestrel-analytics/sre-take-home`, with three commits: compose built from source, the rubric, and the README time box. The exercise has a broken alert rule (`http_requests_total` should be `http_server_requests_total`), a connection leak on 500 responses, and an over-broad S3/IAM policy in Terraform, with a 3-hour limit and no Kubernetes. The rubric has four areas scored 0–3, with no cut-off; the panel is Maya and Noa. `hiring/` has been removed from the infra branch, but only in the working tree, and no PR was opened. Nothing has been sent to the candidate.

- [en-cours] Removal of `hiring/` from `maya/sre-take-home` is uncommitted; the branch will be dropped later.
- [prochaine-étape] After the call on Thursday at 4pm Tel Aviv time, Maya sends the repo invite and the exercise herself.
- [essai-raté] `docker buildx --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 --load` fails because the docker exporter doesn't support manifest lists. The workaround was an arm64-only local build, then building from source in compose.
- [décision] No Kubernetes part; 3-hour maximum; terraform and compose only. (source: t03)
- [décision] `flaky-svc` is built from source in compose, with no prebuilt image published. (source: t06)
- [décision] No pass threshold; scores are input to the panel discussion. Noa is second reviewer. (source: t10)
- [décision] The exercise goes in its own private repo, not in infra. (source: t12)
- [décision] Delete `hiring/` from the infra branch, with no PR in infra. (source: t14)
- [décision] Maya sends the exercise herself after the call; nobody is emailed by the agent. (source: t16)
